title: Store credit that cannot go negative
prompt:
Some regular customers (all fictional, mostly appliances) keep store credit at the shop. Build the `Account` blueprint.

`__init__` stores the owner and the starting balance on `self`. `deposit` adds money. `withdraw` takes money out only if there is enough, and returns `True` when it worked or `False` when it did not.

When it works, the program prints `False`, then `True`, then `Toaster T-9 15`.
hints: In `__init__`, write `self.owner = owner` and do the same for the balance. Without `self.`, the names vanish when `__init__` ends.
`deposit` looks like the counter's click: read `self.balance`, add, store it back.
In `withdraw`, check first: `if amount > self.balance: return False`. Otherwise subtract and `return True`.
explain_after:
Calling `Account("Toaster T-9", 20)` ran `__init__` with those two arguments [py-126]. Each account keeps its own `owner` and `balance`, because instance variables belong to one instance [py-128].

The first withdrawal asked for 30 when the balance was 25, so it returned `False` and changed nothing. The second took 10 and left 15.
